title: Case I — cube with a roof point source
summary: Isolated cube with an ethane point source at the centre of its roof: velocity (laser Doppler, 91 points) and concentration (hydrocarbon analyser, 539 points).

configuration.building: cube, 0.10 m on a side (= H)
configuration.U_H_note: the readme and the velocity sheet; the approach flow at z = H is 1.6969 m/s and the workbook's inflow sheet divides by 1.697
configuration.source: 6 mm circular outlet at the centre of the roof (0, 0, 0.1); 10 % ethane in the mixture, 400 cc/min (= 6.67e-6 m3/s of mixture, 6.67e-7 m3/s of ethane); release velocity 0.236 m/s, M = Ve/UH = 0.14
configuration.reference_concentration: c0 = q / (UH H^2) = 39.22 ppm (39.2 in the paper), q the ETHANE flow; concentration_ratio = C / c0
configuration.instrument: velocity: laser Doppler anemometer (Dantec BSA F60), 200 Hz, 240 s; concentration: hydrocarbon analyser (Kimoto HADA-01), 1 Hz, 120 s
configuration.tunnel: AIST wind tunnel, 20 m long, 3.0 × 2.0 m cross-section; approach flow described as a 1/7 power law (data paper section 3.9)
configuration.scale_note: model scale; the source states no model:full-scale ratio; Eddy3D solves it at 1:60 (a 6 m cube)

frame.origin: the centre of the cube on the ground plane
frame.x: +x streamwise (the wind blows toward +x); the cube spans x in [-0.05, 0.05]; wind points x = -0.15 ... 0.25 m, concentration points x = 0.065 ... 2.7 m
frame.y: +y lateral; the cube spans y in [-0.05, 0.05]; concentration points reach |y| = 0.44 m on the ground
frame.z: +z up; roof at z = 0.1 m; the outlet at (0, 0, 0.1)

inflow_fit.method: log law, kappa = 0.41, least squares over z = 0.02 ... 0.4 m on the workbook's 12-point approach profile
inflow_fit.note: derived during cleaning, not published by AIJ; the workbook's own (z/H)^(1/7) column is within 4.6 % of the measured profile over z = 0.02 ... 0.7 m

fit.method: log law, kappa = 0.41, least squares over z = 0.02 ... 0.4 m on the workbook's 12-point approach profile
fit.note: derived during cleaning, not published by AIJ; the workbook's own (z/H)^(1/7) column is within 4.6 % of the measured profile over z = 0.02 ... 0.7 m

benchmark_data.note: the measured profile and the fit of it are the benchmark's data as cleaned here; everything under `recommended` is a choice

recommended.status: RECOMMENDED by this repository (not part of the benchmark): a log-law inlet fitted to the case's own approach-flow file, with k and epsilon from the standard neutral ABL relations. Any inlet may be submitted; say which in submission.yaml
recommended.profile: U(z) = u*/kappa ln((z + z0)/z0); k = u*^2 / sqrt(Cmu); epsilon = u*^3 / (kappa (z + z0))
recommended.fit: log law, kappa = 0.41, least squares over z = 0.02 ... 0.4 m on the workbook's 12-point approach profile
recommended.openfoam: atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity / atmBoundaryLayerInletK / atmBoundaryLayerInletEpsilon with Uref, Zref, z0 and d = 0; nutkAtmRoughWallFunction with the same z0 on the ground: cases/{id}/inflow_openfoam.txt holds them

flow_direction.meaning: +x is along the wind at WD = 0: flowDir (1 0 0); another WD rotates it about +z by the case's rotation sense (frame.wind_direction_rotation)

inflow.domain: the extents, blockage and cell sizes of Eddy3D's domains are not in its snapshots and are not stated here; mesh.cells and the scale are, where the snapshot has them

probes.columns_meaning: the key columns of a scored file (point_id with config, campaign, instrument, run and wind_direction_deg as the case has them), x, y, z in m (case frame), and scored_as: the families the row is scored in (vector, k, thermistor_bracket, concentration, theta, joined by +)

scoring.U_ref_meaning: U_H, the approach speed at the cube height

scored_as.vector: U, V, W and the speed |U| against the split-fibre, LDV or hot-wire components (velocity.U, velocity.V, velocity.W, speed)
scored_as.thermistor_bracket: a mean scalar speed (thermistor, cup or sonic anemometer) against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar)

scoring.conventions: velocities and the speed over U_ref, k over U_ref^2 (Cases E, F and G publish ratios already); U, V, W, |U| and the thermistor bracket scored as signed velocities (FAC2's ratio keeps the sign; hit rate D = 0.25, W = 0.05); k by the plain definitions (D = 0.25 only); a thermistor, cup or sonic reading (a mean scalar speed) scored against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar), the two ends of its bracket; c* = C/c0 with one detection limit per case, 1e-3 of the largest measured value; theta = (T_floor - T)/(T_floor - T_H) scored like a positive velocity. The same conventions score the served Eddy3D results (docs/validation/method.md).
scoring.tool: python validation/score_submissions.py <folder>, from a checkout of the repository (requirements.txt)

metric_meaning.MeanObserved: mean of the measured, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.MeanPredicted: mean of the modelled, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.Fb: fractional bias, 2 (mean_obs - mean_pred) / (mean_obs + mean_pred); positive = model low
metric_meaning.Fac2: fraction of points within a factor of two (harsh near zero for sign-changing V and W)
metric_meaning.HitRate: fraction of points within D = 0.25 relative or W = 0.05 U_H absolute
metric_meaning.GeometricPairs: pairs with both values positive (used for Mg/Vg)
metric_meaning.null: a metric that is undefined for the data (for example Mg and Vg when no pair has both values positive; Fb, Nmse and Nad of a signed velocity component of Case H or I whose observed and predicted means are not both positive)

known_issues: V on the y = 0 plane (53 of 91 points) is 0 in the CSV and 1e-9 ... 4e-6 m/s in the workbook, a symmetry value. It is NaN in the table; V is measured only at the 38 off-plane points.

The table carries the legacy workbook's values; the CSVs round to 3 decimals (velocity, k) and 1 decimal (concentration, ppm). Every concentration is a multiple of 0.1 ppm: a 0.4 ppm value carries +/-12 % of quantisation.
The paper's c0 = 39.2 ppm needs the ETHANE flow (10 % of the 400 cc/min, 6.67e-7 m3/s); its sentence 'ethane released at 6.67e-6 m3/s' is the mixture. With the mixture flow c0 would be 392 ppm.
The workbook normalises the approach flow with 1.697 m/s and the points with 1.7 m/s (0.18 % apart).
AF_caseI.csv ends in 53 rows of ',,' and two stray cells, '0.5*' and '1.5*' (chart axis labels): a reader that does not test z for a number takes them for data.

Thirteen ground-centreline locations (x, 0, 0) are measured twice (they are on both the y = 0 and the z = 0 plane) with values up to 8.5 % apart; both are kept. The four y = 0, z = 0.05 wind points that appear twice in the workbook are identical copies and appear once.
Only the TKE is published, no variances and no concentration fluctuation: k cannot be checked against the components.
